Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto centres on five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills while creating jobs. They would replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expand apprenticeships, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The manifesto commits to responsible fiscal management, with day-to-day spending not exceeding tax revenue. They propose raising funds through increased taxes on banks, tech giants, and capital gains reform, while prioritising income tax cuts when finances allow.

## Health and Social Care

The party pledges to give everyone the right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) by recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. They would guarantee NHS dental access for urgent care, place mental health professionals in every school, and introduce a 62-day cancer treatment guarantee. For social care, they propose free personal care based on the Scottish model, a higher minimum wage for care workers, and increased support for unpaid carers including paid carer's leave.

## Education

Proposals include increasing school funding above inflation, providing free school meals for all children in poverty, and reinstating maintenance grants for disadvantaged university students. They would put mental health professionals in every school and introduce tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils.

## Housing and Communities

The party targets building 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities. They would ban no-fault evictions, abolish residential leaseholds, and give councils powers to control second homes. They commit to ending rough sleeping within the Parliament.

## Environment

Central proposals include a ten-year home energy upgrade programme, achieving 90% renewable electricity by 2030, and reaching net zero by 2045. They would transform water companies into public benefit companies, ban sewage dumping, and plant 60 million trees annually. A Clean Air Act based on WHO guidelines would be introduced.

## Transport

The manifesto proposes freezing rail fares, extending rail electrification, restoring the 2030 zero-emission vehicle requirement, and expanding electric vehicle charging infrastructure. They would give local authorities more powers over bus services and invest in cycling and walking networks.

## Crime and Justice

Proposals include restoring community policing, guaranteeing police attendance at all burglaries, and creating an Online Crime Agency. They would tackle court backlogs, improve prison rehabilitation, and provide better support for domestic abuse survivors.

## Immigration

The party would scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establish safe legal routes for refugees, and lift the ban on asylum seekers working after three months. They propose transferring work visa policy from the Home Office to relevant departments and reversing family visa income threshold increases.

## Democratic Reform

Key proposals include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, and capping political donations. They would enshrine the Ministerial Code in law, reform the House of Lords, and scrap voter ID requirements.

## International Relations

The party commits to fixing relations with Europe through a four-stage roadmap, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership and eventual EU membership. They would maintain NATO support, increase defence spending toward 2.5% of GDP, reverse Army cuts, and restore international development spending to 0.7% of national income. They advocate for a bilateral ceasefire in Gaza and recognition of Palestinian statehood.
